item.title: Family pays tribute to Yaxley motorcyclist following fatal Sawtry collision
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Family pays tribute to Yaxley motorcyclist following fatal Sawtry collision
The family of 23-year-old Tyler Ellis from Yaxley has paid tribute to him following a fatal collision on the B1043 Old North Road at Sawtry. Mr Ellis was riding a black Kawasaki motorcycle when it collided with a red Volvo HGV at approximately 12:50pm on Monday, October 5. He passed away at Addenbrooke’s Hospital the following day.
The 76-year-old lorry driver from Wisbech was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has since been released on bail until January 4. Cambridgeshire Constabulary is continuing to appeal for witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage of the incident to come forward by calling 101 or visiting the force's website.

item.title: King’s Lynn Rotary club donates £500 to support Kolkata street children
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Rotary club donates £500 to support Kolkata street children
A King’s Lynn couple has received a £500 donation from the local Priory Rotary Club to support The Hope Foundation for Street Children. Dr Prabir Mitra and his wife Sanjukta recently completed a 111-day, 28,200-mile road journey from King’s Lynn to Kolkata.
The pair travelled through Europe, Central Asia, China, Tibet, and Nepal, crossing 20 international borders. During the trip, they raised awareness about diabetes and collected funds for a dialysis unit at The Hope Hospital in Kolkata. The Rotary donation will assist the foundation in providing education and protection for street children. The couple faced numerous challenges during their expedition, including difficult road conditions and frequent border closures.

item.title: Wigan man fined following assault at King’s Lynn nightclub
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wigan man fined following assault at King’s Lynn nightclub
A holidaymaker has been ordered to pay compensation and fines after assaulting a security guard in King’s Lynn. Forty-nine-year-old Matthew Crompton, from Wigan, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He admitted to a charge of assault by beating following an incident at Dr Thirsty’s nightclub on Norfolk Street in the early hours of Sunday, September 6.
The court heard that Crompton, who was visiting the area, punched a member of door staff in the face after being ejected from the venue. His solicitor stated that the punch was intended for a different guard. Crompton must pay £300 in compensation, a £750 fine, a £300 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

Man charged following incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station
A 34-year-old man has been charged with assaulting three police officers following an incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station. Reuben Skinner, of Checker Street in Lynn, faces three counts of assault after officers were called to reports of a man with a head injury on Saturday evening.
Police have confirmed that no weapons were involved in the incident, dismissing online speculation regarding a stabbing. Mr Skinner was arrested at the station and later taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital for treatment. He has been released on bail and is due to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 19. Enquiries into how the man sustained his initial injury remain ongoing.

New £110,000 annual fund launched for Cambridgeshire families
A new financial support scheme has been announced for families across Cambridgeshire. Council leader Rayo confirmed that a fund worth £110,000 per year is being established to provide timely assistance to local households. The initiative aims to offer support to those in need throughout the region.
